name: unknown_provider
summary: No reducer claims this provider and endpoint, so the bytes cannot be read as a turn.
trigger: Provider and endpoint resolved, and no registered reducer handles the pair.
grounding: The set of provider shapes capture can read is a property of the build, and it is contract because it decides which traffic becomes sessions: an implementation with a reducer the other lacks captures turns the other silently does not. A turn refused for this reason is a coverage gap rather than a defect in the traffic, which is why it is worth its own reason — it is the counter an operator reads to find out that a provider went unwatched.
not_expressible: The answer depends on which reducers a build registers, which is exactly the thing that differs between implementations. A case pinning the current set would assert the reducer registry rather than the rule that an unclaimed shape is refused rather than guessed at.
notes: This is the reason a NEW provider produces before it is supported, so a nonzero count is the signal to add a reducer, not to fix the traffic.
